descricao_original: The cap stage results from a differential rate of cell proliferation in the epithelial cells of the bud, resulting in a concave structure resembling a cup. During this stage, histodifferentiation occurs establishing the enamel organ which encloses ectomesenchymal cells that develop into the dental papilla. The dental papilla forms the dentin and pulp. 400x
creditos_identificados: Image source: This image was taken of a slide in the University of South Dakota slide collection.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The tooth germ is first identifiable at the cap stage of tooth development (histodifferentiation). The tooth germ consists of all the identifiable ectoderm and ectomesenchyme tissues that form the tooth: inner and outer enamel epithelia, (ectoderm), dental papillae and the dental follicle (ectomesenchyme).
